story.title: In Harat Al Busaid, Eighty Elders Gather to Keep the Memory of Adam Alive

detail.extracted_title: In Harat Al Busaid, Eighty Elders Gather to Keep the Memory of Adam Alive
detail.excerpt: Organized by the Al Jami' Team of Al Bashaer Club, an intergenerational gathering in Wilayat Adam brought together eighty elders to share oral histories, folk proverbs, and the lived history of Ad Dakhiliyah's ancient quarters.
detail.article_html:
When eighty elders sit together in the historic quarter of Harat Al Busaid in Wilayat Adam, the conversation quickly turns into a living archive. Yesterday, the Al Jami' Team—affiliated with Al Bashaer Club—organized a community gathering for the wilayat's senior residents in Ad Dakhiliyah Governorate, held under the patronage of Dr. Mohammed bin Ali Al Mahri, Wali of Adam, and attended by younger residents and local heritage researchers.

The gathering was designed with a straightforward purpose: to bring older and younger generations into the same room, strengthen neighborhood bonds, and record the social and cultural memory of Adam before its spoken details fade.

Poetry, Folk Proverbs, and Ancestral Wisdom

The program opened with traditional poetry recitations honoring the place of elders (kibar al-sin) as the moral and historical anchors of Omani society. From there, attention turned to the architectural and social history of Wilayat Adam and its ancient haras (walled quarters), tracing how families organized water, trade, and communal life across decades.

One of the liveliest moments of the day was a competition centered on traditional Omani folk proverbs (amthal sha'biyah). Each proverb served as a doorway into the practical wisdom and lived experiences passed down by parents and grandparents—short, memorable phrases shaped by agriculture, desert travel, and shared community responsibility.

Open Dialogue Circles on How Life in Adam Changed

At the heart of the meeting were open dialogue sessions in which the elders spoke directly about their own lives. They recounted the social, economic, and urban transformations that Wilayat Adam has experienced over the past century—from the days of mud-brick compounds and shared falaj routines to modern neighborhoods.

Throughout their stories, the elders returned to the enduring Omani values that held the old quarters together: mutual aid (takaful), cooperation, and the obligations of good neighborliness (husn al-jiwar). For the young people listening in Harat Al Busaid, those oral accounts offered a firsthand connection to the daily rhythms and resilience of their forebears, ensuring that Adam's unwritten stories remain part of the town's present identity.

detail.instagram_caption:
In the historic quarter of Harat Al Busaid in Wilayat Adam, 80 senior residents gathered to pass down the spoken memory of their town to younger generations. Organized by the Al Jami' Team of Al Bashaer Club under the patronage of Dr. Mohammed bin Ali Al Mahri, Wali of Adam, the meeting turned a traditional courtyard into a living classroom of Ad Dakhiliyah's heritage.

Through poetry recitations, a competition in traditional Omani folk proverbs, and open dialogue circles, the elders recounted how life in Adam's ancient haras evolved across decades of social, economic, and architectural change.

Their accounts highlighted the daily practices of mutual aid, cooperation, and good neighborliness that sustained Omani communities for generations—preserving oral histories directly from those who lived them.

Read the full analysis at omanspire.om (link in bio).
